Score Cells by Cell Cycle Phase

Source: R/runCellCycle.R
runCellCycle.Rd

Assigns each cell an S-phase score, a G2/M score and a phase call, using the Tirosh et al. marker sets that ship with Seurat and Seurat::CellCycleScoring(). The marker lists are human symbols; for any other organism they are converted to that species' orthologs first, so the same call works across species without the caller assembling gene lists.

Usage

runCellCycle(
  obj,
  organism = c("hsa", "mmu", "rno", "dre"),
  method = c("gprofiler", "homologene", "babelgene")
)

Arguments

obj

A single Seurat object, normalised.

organism

Three-letter code selecting the marker set: "hsa" (human, the default) uses Seurat::cc.genes directly; "mmu" (mouse), "rno" (rat) and "dre" (zebrafish) convert it to orthologs first.

method

Ortholog mapping backend passed to orthogene::convert_orthologs(). "gprofiler" (the default) is the most complete but needs network access; "homologene" and "babelgene" resolve locally. Ignored when organism = "hsa".

Value

The input object with S.Score, G2M.Score and Phase added to its metadata. Cell count and identities are unchanged. The data layer is unchanged too, unless the object arrived unnormalised – see Normalisation.

Details

Cell cycle is a QC concern because it is one of the largest sources of variation in a proliferating population, and it is structured variation – cycling cells cluster with cycling cells regardless of type. The scores are added here so that they can be looked at, and if necessary regressed out later; nothing is regressed, scaled or clustered by this function.

What gets added

Seurat::CellCycleScoring() writes three metadata columns:

S.Score, G2M.Score

Mean expression of each marker set, centred against a background of control features drawn from comparable expression bins. Relative, not absolute: a score near zero means "no more than the background", not "no expression".

Phase

"S", "G2M" or "G1", from whichever score is higher, with "G1" when both are negative. "G1" therefore also absorbs G0 – the two are not separable from these markers.

Idents() is deliberately left alone (set.ident = FALSE), so the sample identity seuratFrom10x() set survives.

Normalisation

Scoring bins genes by average expression, which assumes the data have been normalised. An object that still looks like raw counts is normalised here with Seurat::NormalizeData() at its defaults, after a warning – and the returned object carries that normalised data, since scoring against one version of the data and handing back another would be worse than either.

Normalise beforehand if you want anything other than the defaults; the check is a heuristic (log-normalised values are essentially never whole numbers), so an already-normalised object is left exactly as it was.

The installed Seurat version is detected automatically. Seurat 4 copies the counts into the data slot when an object is created, so the heuristic reads that copy. A Seurat 5 object has no data layer until it is normalised, so its absence alone means raw. Seurat 5 objects whose layers are still split by sample after a merge are read across every layer.

Non-human organisms

Markers are converted with orthogene::convert_orthologs(), which is only needed – and only loaded – when organism is not "hsa". Genes without a one-to-one ortholog are dropped, so the converted sets are smaller than the human ones; how many survived is reported.

The default conversion method, "gprofiler", queries a web service and so needs network access. On a machine without it, pass method = "homologene", which resolves locally from a bundled mapping at the cost of some coverage.

See also

Seurat::CellCycleScoring() for the scoring itself, diagnoseQC() for the other per-cell QC metrics.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
seurat <- mergeSeurat(seuratFrom10x(path = "/path/to/Pool1/outs", multi = TRUE))
seurat <- Seurat::NormalizeData(seurat)

seurat <- runCellCycle(seurat, organism = "mmu")

table(seurat$Phase)

# is one sample cycling harder than the others?
table(seurat$Ident, seurat$Phase)

# on a cluster with no outbound network
seurat <- runCellCycle(seurat, organism = "mmu", method = "homologene")

# the scores are ordinary metadata, so they plot like any other metric
plotScatter(seurat, "S.Score", "G2M.Score", group_by = "Phase")
} # }
